chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Marriage is only annulled (returned) due to leprosy, and leprosy, and madness, and blindness."

key_terms.اَلْجُذَامِ: leprosy (specifically Hansen's disease or dark leprosy)
key_terms.يُرَدُّ: annulled or returned (in the context of marriage contract)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific defects that allow for marriage annulment in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *ta’dil* (evaluation of defects) in Shia marriage jurisprudence, limiting annulment to four specific conditions: leprosy (*al-baras*), severe leprosy (*al-judham*), madness (*al-junun*), and blindness (*al-'afal*). Unlike some Sunni schools that may include other defects, this narration emphasizes that only these distinct physical and mental impairments constitute valid grounds for returning the marriage, reflecting the juristic focus on significant impediments to marital life.
